title: ENTRY live monitoring as the demotion signal (not an edge lever): live ENTRY closes vs the dev/held-out band, rule written before use
note: RULE (written before the first live read, operator 2026-11-01: ENTRY goes live on bybit_2 as approved). Expected band from dev/held-out: traded-5 -0.041 net R per decision (dev, 4 seeds, n about 5.5k each); pooled frozen-60 +0.007 (dev and held-out); October 2026 -0.019R (manager). Evaluate realised net R per closed ENTRY decision (full cost stack: fees, slippage, funding) per account over ALL its closed ENTRY trades, every 50 closes once n >= 100. FLAG ENTRY_LIVE_NEGATIVE when mean + 2*SE < 0 (SE = SD/sqrt(n)): the live loss is statistically real. FLAG ENTRY_LIVE_BELOW_DEV when mean < -0.041 - 2*SE: worse than even the weak traded-5 dev reading. A flag is a realtime ping to the operator with the numbers; it demotes nothing by itself (no halting; a demotion is the mirror-window rule's, and the operator's). Reads only closed trades; sizes nothing. Tier 2 because it adds a standing read on the live ENTRY legs. Gates this adds: none (a flag, not a switch). [2026-11-04 lane ML-ENTRY-RETRAIN-MONITOR] BUILT report-only: src/runtime/ml_entry_live_monitor.py implements the rule exactly as written (n>=100, checkpoint every 50 closes, mean+2SE<0 => ENTRY_LIVE_NEGATIVE, mean<-0.041-2SE => ENTRY_LIVE_BELOW_DEV, sample SD, per account over all closed strategy_name=ml_entry rows, net R via net_r_label.net_r_for_trade = gross - taker - maker - funding over SL-distance risk). Operational exit reasons (the NOT_STRATEGY_EXIT vocabulary incl. operator_flatten_reconciled, so bybit_2 6844/6845 drop out) are excluded and counted; R-uncomputable and uncosted rows are counted, never zeroed. Hourly tick in src/main.py (best-effort, no broker call), ping via the losing_streak shape, read surface /api/diag/log_file?name=ml_entry_live_monitor_state, brief_line() for the brief. A flag halts/demotes/sizes nothing. 14 tests incl. exact-threshold, checkpoint idempotence, vocabulary equality with real_money_close_attribution. NOT verified: the live journal (no access from this sandbox); strategy_name='ml_entry' is the value strategies.yaml and soak_state use, confirm on the first read. FIRST OBSERVATION: after deploy, /api/diag/log_file?name=ml_entry_live_monitor_state shows __last_check__ newer than the trader start and bybit_2 {n, state}; the first VERDICT is the first checkpoint at n=100 graded closes on an account (insufficient_n until then is 'no verdict', not a pass). [2026-11-04 ~20:08Z OPERATOR DECISION via Manager Session 2026-11-04a, popup verbatim] "Merge when green (Recommended)" for PR #22942 (retrain workflow + report-only live monitor). Landing hold stays, merge-slot claim committed; manager merges and deploys in tonight combined trader restart. [2026-11-06 ~16:00Z lane] The served-model stale grade (409.9 d, limit 22 d) cannot clear by itself: a green weekly retrain does not change the served artifact, so the freshness line stays stale until a candidate-to-served path exists. Proposal HELD in PR #23859 (graded swap: candidate vs served on the same post-train window, deflated holdout_lock bar, net of costs; pass opens a draft replace PR, fail keeps the old artifact and raises one flag). Tier 2 serving path + Tier 3 model replacement: needs the manager/operator. [2026-11-06 ~16:30Z lane] First grade of the weekly candidate vs the served model on the same 2026-10-23..11-05 window (net of the full cost stack): served v1 mean -0.0918 R/decision (n 342, se 0.059) -- negative; candidate refit as of 10-23 +0.0018 (n 281). Longs lose on both (served -0.57 at n 42, candidate -0.73 at n 69); shorts are -0.03 (served, n 300) vs +0.24 (candidate, n 212): post-hoc cuts of one read, not findings. Served-model freshness stays stale until PR #23859 lands a pass; verdict was insufficient_n. [2026-11-06 ~17:15Z lane] Monitor freshness limit FRESH_MAX_AGE_DAYS 22 -> 35 (operator 'Raise to 35 days (Recommended)', ~17:02Z; report-only), in HELD #23859 (38602e206) and carried by #23888. Why: a graded candidate is a refit as of run_date-14 d with the 7d+25h embargo, so it is ~22-23 d old on the day it can be promoted; 22 would label every promoted model stale at once. The monitor test that depended on the real repo artifact being 408 d stale now uses a tmp artifact (it would have broken once the pointer moves). After #23888 merges and the trader restarts the monitor should read the new model id and data_through 2026-10-14 19:00Z (~23 d, fresh under 35); the monitor remains the demotion signal and nothing about it gates a trade.
